root_cause.hypothesis: The read pointer increment is gated by the raw request rd_en (line 71: `if (rd_en) rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;`) instead of the accepted-read qualifier rd_fire (rd_en && !empty). When the FIFO is empty and rd_en is held high (the underflow test), the read is correctly dropped for rd_data (rd_fire=0) but rd_ptr still advances. At the edge at 435000 ps, wr_ptr=0000 and rd_ptr=0000 (empty=1, rd_fire=0, underflow=1), yet rd_ptr moved to 0001, so count = wr_ptr - rd_ptr wrapped to 1111 (15) and empty deasserted. From then on the DUT believes it holds 15 entries: rd_fire becomes 1, stale memory (mem[1]=0x0a, ...) is read out on rd_data, and underflow is no longer flagged, causing all subsequent count/empty/underflow/rd_data errors in the underflow and wraparound tests.

evidence.interpretation: Write pointer before the failing edge; unchanged since 315000, no writes in the underflow phase.
rd_ptr == wr_ptr before edge 435000: FIFO genuinely empty.
DUT correctly reports empty before the failing edge.
A read is requested while empty.
Read correctly not accepted (rd_en && !empty = 0); rd_ptr must therefore hold.
Dropped read correctly flagged before the edge.
No concurrent write, so nothing should change at edge 435000.
rd_ptr advanced despite rd_fire=0 at the edge: the divergence point.
count = 0000 - 0001 wraps to 15; matches the first ERROR (got 0xf expected 0x0).
empty deasserts because pointers no longer match; matches ERROR empty got 0x0.
rd_data correctly held (0x10) at the failing edge since rd_fire was 0; the data path itself is gated correctly.
Increment at 425000 is a legal read (count 1->0); increments at 435000 and 445000 occur while FIFO should be empty.
wr_ptr constant at 0000 throughout the window.
count reaches 0 then wraps to 15 and decrements: underflow of the pointer difference.
rd_fire was 0 during cycle 425000-435000 yet rd_ptr incremented at 435000; afterwards rd_fire=1 only because the corrupted pointers make the FIFO look non-empty.
At 445000 stale data 0x0a (mem[1]) is read out: consequence of the corrupted rd_ptr; matches ERROR rd_data got 0xa expected 0x10 at 446000.
Stale storage word at address 1 equals the bogus rd_data value, confirming the read was from rd_ptr[2:0]=1.

alternative_hypotheses_considered: count/empty derivation (lines 53, 56) wrong: rejected - both are correct functions of the pointers; wr_ptr=0000/rd_ptr=0001 really gives 1111 and empty=0, so the pointers themselves are corrupted.
rd_fire definition (line 51) wrong: rejected - rd_fire was 0 at 434000 with rd_en=1/empty=1, exactly per spec.
rd_data update gating (line 69-70) wrong: rejected - rd_data held 0x10 across the dropped read at edge 435000; rd_data errors only start after the pointer was corrupted.
Write-side bug (wr_ptr/wr_fire/mem write): rejected - wr_en=0 and wr_ptr unchanged throughout the window; tests fill/drain/overflow passed.
Testbench/reference model error: rejected - spec states reads while empty are dropped; DUT's own rd_fire/underflow agree the read was dropped, yet rd_ptr moved.
limitations: Diagnosis is a hypothesis supported by waveform evidence and RTL inspection, not a formal proof. The fix (gate rd_ptr increment with rd_fire) was not simulated, since re-running the simulator was disallowed. Only the window around the first failure was examined in detail; later errors (wraparound test, etc.) are attributed to the same cause by inference.
